earnings.title: MPLX LP Reports Third-Quarter 2026 Financial Results;
highlights: Third-quarter net income attributable to MPLX of $1.2 billion and net cash provided by operating activities of $1.5 billion
FINDLAY, Ohio, Nov. 3, 2026 - MPLX LP (NYSE: MPLX) today reported third-quarter 2026 net income attributable to MPLX of $1,164 million, compared with $1,545 million for the third quarter of 2025.
Net income attributable to MPLX LP $ 1,164 $ 1,545 $ 3,153 $ 3,719
Adjusted EBITDA attributable to MPLX of $1.9 billion and distributable cash flow of $1.5 billion, enabling the return of $1.1 billion of capital
During the quarter, MPLX generated $1,477 million in net cash provided by operating activities, $1,537 million of distributable cash flow, and adjusted free cash flow of $447 million.

quotes.text: Our third-quarter results reflect strong execution and the continued progression of our integrated natural gas and NGL value chain growth strategy. The durability of our cash flows enabled us to increase our quarterly distribution by 12.5% for the third consecutive year.
quotes.by: Maryann Mannen, MPLX chairman, president and chief executive officer

outlook: Paul Park and Mandan refineries, MPLX announced the sale of associated logistics assets for $750 million, representing a 9x multiple on forecast 2027 adjusted EBITDA.

items.heading: A significant decrease in crude oil and natural gas production in our areas of operation may adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash available for distribution.
We may not always be able to accurately estimate expected production volumes of our producer customers; therefore, volumes we service in the future could be less than we anticipate.

We depend on third parties for the crude oil, natural gas and refined products we gather, transport and store, the natural gas we process, and the NGLs we fractionate and stabilize at our facilities, and a reduction in these quantities could reduce our revenues and cash flow.
We may not be able to retain existing customers, or acquire new customers, which would reduce our revenues and limit our future profitability.

The fees charged to third parties under our gathering, treating, processing, transmission, transportation, fractionation, stabilization and storage agreements may not escalate sufficiently to cover increases in costs, or the agreements may not be renewed or may be suspended in some circumstances.
The U.S. inland waterway infrastructure is aging and may result in increased costs and disruptions to our operations.
